description: GNU Bash shell — navigation, file handling, text, variables and scripting.

pwd.title: Current directory
pwd.description: Prints the absolute path of the current working directory.

cd.title: Change directory
cd.description: Changes the current working directory. With no arguments it goes to HOME; 'cd -' goes back to the previous one.

ls.title: List files
ls.description: Lists directory contents in long format, including hidden files and human-readable sizes.
arguments: Includes hidden files (starting with a dot).

cp.title: Copy files
cp.description: Copies files or directories; -r copies directories recursively.
warnings: Without -i, cp overwrites the destination silently.

mv.title: Move or rename
mv.description: Moves or renames files and directories. It is the standard way to rename in the shell.
warnings: Silently overwrites the destination if it already exists.

rm-rf.title: Remove recursively
rm-rf.description: Removes files and directories recursively without confirmation. Irreversible.
warnings: There is no trash: removal is permanent.
Never run 'rm -rf /' or use it with empty variables (e.g. rm -rf $DIR/).

mkdir-p.title: Create directories
mkdir-p.description: Creates directories; -p creates intermediate ones and does not fail if they already exist.

find.title: Find files
find.description: Walks the directory tree searching by name, type, size or date.
examples: Removes .tmp files modified more than 7 days ago.
arguments: Runs a command for each result.

grep.title: Search text
grep.description: Finds lines matching a pattern (regex), recursively and case-insensitively.
arguments: Inverts: lines that do NOT match.

sed.title: Replace text (sed)
sed.description: Stream editor. With -i it edits the file in place, replacing all occurrences.
warnings: -i modifies the original file; on macOS it requires a suffix: sed -i ''.

awk.title: Process columns (awk)
awk.description: Processes text by fields/columns. Ideal for extracting and formatting tabular data.
examples: Lists users using ':' as the field separator.

tail-f.title: Follow a file
tail-f.description: Shows the end of a file and keeps following new lines (useful for logs).
arguments: Follows the file in real time.

pipe.title: Chain commands (pipe)
pipe.description: Chains commands by feeding the output of one as the input of the next.

redirect.title: Redirect output
redirect.description: Redirects stdout to a file; 2>&1 sends stderr too. '>>' appends instead of overwriting.
examples: Appends to the end of the file.
warnings: '>' overwrites the destination file without warning.

xargs.title: Build commands (xargs)
xargs.description: Reads items from standard input and passes them as arguments to another command.
examples: Use -print0/-0 to safely handle spaces in names.
arguments: Replaces {} with the item on each run.
warnings: Chained with rm/mv it can delete many files at once.

export.title: Environment variable
export.description: Sets a variable and exports it to the shell's child processes.
warnings: Don't export secrets into a shared history; prefer .env files kept out of version control.

command-substitution.title: Command substitution
command-substitution.description: Captures a command's output into a variable using $(...).

for-loop.title: for loop
for-loop.description: Iterates over a list of items (files, words, sequences) running commands.
examples: Iterates from 1 to 5 using brace expansion.

if.title: if conditional
if.description: Runs commands conditionally. [ -f ] tests for a file; [ -d ] tests for a directory; [ -z ] tests for an empty string.
warnings: Always quote variables in tests: [ -n "$VAR" ] avoids errors with empty values.

function.title: Define a function
function.description: Creates a reusable function in the script or interactive shell; $1..$n are the arguments.

shebang.title: Shebang and set -euo
shebang.description: Recommended script header: sets the interpreter and enables strict mode (errors, unset variables and pipe failures abort).
arguments: Errors when using an unset variable.
Fails if any step of the pipe fails.

chmod-x.title: Make executable
chmod-x.description: Adds execute permission to a file so it can be run directly.
warnings: Avoid 'chmod 777'; grant only the permissions needed.

ps-kill.title: Processes and kill
ps-kill.description: Lists running processes. Combine with kill <PID> to terminate a process.
examples: Forces termination (SIGKILL) — use as a last resort.
warnings: kill -9 doesn't let the process save its state; try kill (SIGTERM) first.
